description: We're a team interested in space, science, and technology, bringing skills in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, IoT, UI/UX design, and creative problem-solving. We also value communication, research, and presentation. We're looking to bring our different strengths together, learn from one another, and build something innovative for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We welcome curious, motivated people who are ready to collaborate, experiment, and have fun!
summary:
Know Your Kerala is an interactive rainfall data explorer developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge’s Earth System Trend Detective challenge. The project transforms NASA satellite-based precipitation data into an accessible, visual investigation of Kerala’s rainfall patterns. Through an interactive dashboard, users can explore rainfall statistics across different time periods, examine monthly and seasonal patterns, and investigate long-term trends using the Mann–Kendall statistical test and Sen’s slope estimator.

By presenting scientific data through an approachable interface and clear visual explanations, the project helps make Earth system data easier for the public to understand and explore. Its regional focus connects large-scale satellite observations to a place familiar to its intended audience. Rather than treating a statistical trend as a definitive prediction, Know Your Kerala encourages curiosity, evidence-based investigation, and a deeper understanding of rainfall variability in Kerala.
details:
Know Your Kerala is a public-facing rainfall data explorer designed to make NASA Earth observation data more accessible and meaningful at a regional scale. The project focuses on Kerala, India, and uses monthly precipitation records from NASA’s Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission, specifically the IMERG dataset.

Users can interact with the website to explore rainfall across different time periods. The dashboard presents total precipitation, monthly mean rainfall, the wettest calendar month, and an interactive rainfall timeline. A seasonal visualization helps users investigate how rainfall varies throughout the year. To examine long-term patterns, the project calculates annual rainfall totals from complete calendar years and applies the Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope estimator to assess trend direction, magnitude, and statistical significance.

The project’s intended impact is to bridge the gap between complex scientific datasets and everyday users. By focusing on Kerala and presenting information through clear visualizations and plain-language explanations, it encourages the public to investigate local environmental patterns and ask evidence-based questions.

Creativity is central to the project’s approach. Instead of presenting data as a conventional scientific dashboard, Know Your Kerala aims to combine data exploration with an illustration-led visual identity inspired by Kerala’s monsoon landscapes. The design connects the rhythm of rainfall with the visual and cultural character of the region.

The project was developed using JavaScript, React, Vite, CSS, PapaParse for CSV processing, and Recharts for interactive visualizations. Statistical calculations are implemented in JavaScript. Key considerations include data accuracy, completeness of annual records, readability, responsive design, accessibility, and responsible interpretation of statistical results. The project does not claim that a detected trend alone proves climate change or predicts future rainfall.
